payload.body:
exam (task 1, tests/test_compile_plan_dependencies.py) — approach.

One pytest file in the shape of tests/test_compile_plan_edges.py: a real one-task claims-v1 plan written to tmp_path with its gate-verdict record written by extract_gate_input.gate_input, parameterized on the header **Dependencies:** line, compiled by a subprocess and read off stdout / the --emit-args file / the exit code / stderr. Legs (a)-(f) call the two module-level functions directly (sys.path.insert on skills/ultrapowers/scripts, then compile_plan.parse_dependencies / compile_plan.dependencies_violations), so BASE fails them as AttributeError on the absent name rather than as an ImportError on the module.

Verified at BASE: the template plan checks PLAN OK and compiles rc 0 both with and without the header line — so the header line is inert at BASE and every red below is the absent feature, not a malformed fixture. evals/fixtures/claims/plan.md compiles rc 0 with --emit-launch/--emit-args (leg (h) is the one leg green at BASE, being the no-key case).

Two readings I am pinning, so a later session does not have to reconstruct them:

1. Leg (i)/M4 say --check prints the refusal on STDERR. Every other --check violation in this compiler goes to STDOUT (main() line ~2932 prints collect_violations' strings with a bare print; only the plain-compile grammar path at ~3049 uses file=sys.stderr). The Proof says stderr, so the exam asserts stderr, and the implementer must route the dependencies: strings there under --check as well. I am not substituting stdout for it: that would leave M4 unproven. Flagging it here because it is the one place this task's clause diverges from the house shape.

2. Leg (f) 'yields a string beginning dependencies: naming dev: twice' — read as: the both-dev defect yields exactly one string, beginning dependencies:, that names the dev: marker. The exam asserts len==1, the prefix, and that dev: appears in it; it does not pin a count of the substring inside the message, which would be pinning wording the clause does not give. The both-empty message is asserted as one dependencies: string matching (?i)no package|empty, for the same reason.

payload.body: Done and committed. All five PROOFS green; full pytest suite 351 passed. Decision a later session would otherwise rediscover: M4 pins the M2 refusal strings to STDERR, but --check's own verdict list has always printed on stdout (collect_violations -> print(); 'N violation(s)'). So dependencies_violations is joined into collect_violations like every other species — it counts toward the verdict and keeps --check from printing PLAN OK on a defective line — and the --check branch ADDITIONALLY mirrors just those strings onto stderr. That means a defective Dependencies line appears on both channels under --check; launch.mjs's verifyPlanCompiles reads output(res), which carries both, so the launcher refusal is unchanged either way. Second decision: a second 'dev:' word is a refusal, not a second split — parse_dependencies keeps the extra marker out of the dev list rather than re-partitioning, so the violation names it. Third: the compiled key is written only when the header carries the line, in both the stdout result and args_payload; the launch file deliberately does not carry it (M3 names only the two).

payload.body:
Exam written: `fleet/tests/test_run_engine_declared_dependencies.mjs` (985 lines), red at BASE on leg (a) — `driver:dependencies` events: `[]`. Verified with a soft-assert copy that every one of the 41 assertions that fails at BASE fails for the absent implementation (no add line, no setup commit, no `report.setupSha`, no park, no manifest red, no doc sentences) — none for a fixture, an import or a typo. Legs (j) and the direct `bootstrapManifestChanged` reads pass at BASE by design: they are the no-change clause M7.

Three readings a later session would otherwise have to reconstruct (all three are stated in the file header too):

1. LEG (e) NEEDS A SECOND CAPTURE, and the leg's own action is kept. The leg reads `$ULTRA_BASE` out of the FOLDED tree via a proof `Run:` of `echo $ULTRA_BASE > ultra-base.txt`. Measured against this tree at BASE: that `Run:` executes during `prePass`, which happens AFTER both the `withPatchCapture` wrapper capture and the exam-handoff re-capture — so on a task that goes green on its first pass the file never reaches the patch or the fold. The action named by the leg is unchanged (same `Run:`, same variable, same file, read off the folded tree); what the exam adds is a fixture device beside it: task A carries a SECOND `Run:`, `test -f fix-ran.txt`, red at iter 0, so the `fix:A:0` round the red buys re-captures the clone and carries the first pass's `ultra-base.txt` into the patch. This is a fixture, not a substituted action (#836) — the bytes compared are still what the driver's own `$ULTRA_BASE` wrote.

2. THE SEVENTH `Run:` IS NOT SPAWNED. `node fleet/tests/test_run_engine_lockfile_regen.mjs` is the driver's to run; the hermetic-sims constraint forbids a sim spawning a sibling sim. Standing in for it in-file: leg (j) — a task whose `files` LIST `package.json` and that edits it draws no red, with and without `dependencies` — which is exactly the exemption that sim's two tasks (`files: ['package.json','bun.lock']`) rely on, plus direct `bootstrapManifestChanged` reads (accepts `client/package.json`, refuses `package.json.bak`). No `unsatisfiable` entry: nothing about leg (l) is unencodable, only that one command belongs to the driver.

3. TWO M2 READINGS PINNED. (i) `bun.lock` is untracked at BASE and the canned `add.sh` WRITES it, so leg (c2)'s 'both paths in the commit' is only satisfiable if 'every path `git status --porcelain` reports' includes the `??` ones — the exam asserts the commit carries exactly `['bun.lock','package.json']` and not `node_modules/marker`. (ii) M2's body is read as ONE line, `setup: dependencies left-pad@^1 right-pad dev: eslint`, because the clause writes the dev half as ` dev: <dev specs>` with a leading space rather than as a new line; specs are space-joined. An implementer who writes the dev half on a second line will see leg (c2) red on the body compare.

payload.author: impl:3@run-170
payload.body:
Landed at db995e9c. Setup reads args.dependencies/addCmd/addDevCmd, runs one shell line in the integration clone after the #383 reuse block and before the baseline clone is cut, stages only manifest BASENAMES (bootstrapManifestChanged) and commits under the plan H1. setupHead threads through adoptedHead, patchBase.current, the baseline checkout and both $ULTRA_BASE sites; report.baseSha stays the launch BASE and report.setupSha is new. A non-zero exit reuses the parkedOnBaseline latch via parkAtSetup (why: setup), which already short-circuits claimEpoch/foldEpoch/the lane loop, so no worker of any label is dispatched; the tail loop got an `else if (!parkedOnBaseline)` guard so its rows are not duplicated (byte-equivalent at BASE). manifestReds runs last in prePass, exempting paths the task Files declare.

One trap worth flagging for anyone touching this area: the engine git() wrapper TRIMS stdout, which is wrong for `git status --porcelain` — the first field is two status chars that may both be a space (" M bun.lock"), so a trim eats the leading one and every path reads short by one char. Used raw exec() there instead. Caught only because a sim leg asserted bun.lock was in the setup commit.
